title: Superconductivity in High-Entropy Alloy System Containing Tb

questions.broad: In high-entropy alloys, what governs superconducting behavior and why? Formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis, identify a controlled comparison against a baseline that could reveal the governing cause, predict the relative observations expected if the hypothesis is correct, define its boundary conditions, state what prior evidence would make it plausible, and specify a result that would falsify it.
questions.problem_constrained: For a selected high-entropy alloy whose superconducting behavior remains uncharacterized, what governs whether and how superconductivity emerges in the low-temperature test regime, and why? Propose one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison with the starting state, the observations expected relative to that baseline, the limits over which the hypothesis should hold, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.
questions.expert_context: Reported superconducting high-entropy alloys are dominated by Nb-Ta matrices, while other studies concern titanium-rich systems based on heavy transition metals and partly ordered systems. Consequently, these precedents do not establish what controls superconductivity in high-entropy alloys outside the best-studied material classes. Within the defining constraint of a solid solution containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each, what governs superconducting behavior in such an uncharacterized high-entropy alloy, and why? State one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison against the starting material, predicted observations relative to the baseline, applicable boundary conditions, the earlier evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an outcome that would falsify it.

gap.evidence: there is no information about superconductivity in a system containing lanthanides which crystallize in a bcc structure
gap.reason: The introduction identifies a missing understanding of superconducting behavior in lanthanide-containing, bcc-structured systems, rather than a material performance target or a limitation of measurement or modeling methods.
